Take absolute values and use $|f'(c)|\le M$:

For $x=y$ both sides are $0$, so the inequality also holds. $\blacksquare$

reference_proof:
The partial sums $S_n=\sum_{k=1}^n \dfrac{1}{k^2}$ form an increasing sequence (all terms positive).
For $k\ge 2$, use the telescoping bound $\dfrac{1}{k^2}\le \dfrac{1}{k(k-1)}=\dfrac{1}{k-1}-\dfrac{1}{k}$. Hence
$$S_n\le 1+\sum_{k=2}^n\Big(\frac{1}{k-1}-\frac1k\Big)=1+\Big(1-\frac1n\Big)<2.$$
$\{S_n\}$ is increasing and bounded above by $2$, so it converges by the monotone convergence theorem. $\blacksquare$
hint_ladder: The partial sums increase, so only an upper bound is missing; the key is the monotone convergence theorem.
